svg.text: Filled orange: direct gap (a photon can cross it on its own); grey ring: indirect (it needs a lattice vibration too, so light emission is about a million times slower than the competing
non-radiative losses). Notice that Si and C are indirect, while GaAs, InP, GaN and the Zn and Cd chalcogenides (ZnSe, CdTe) are direct: that is why LEDs and lasers are III-V or II-VI,
not silicon. The rock-salt alkaline-earth chalcogenides (CaO, SrS) are indirect, and the alkali halides are direct but insulators, their gaps far in the ultraviolet. Caveat: PBE gaps are
too small (Si 1.12 eV measured, GaAs 1.42, GaN 3.4), so read colours and positions as relative; the direct/indirect character is more reliable than the value.
